title: Labour Loses 35 Councils and 1,300+ Seats in Historic Local Election Defeat
detail: Results from the 7 May 2026 local elections confirmed Labour's most severe mid-term electoral collapse since its 2024 general election landslide. Labour lost control of 35 councils and over 1,300 council seats across England, with support collapsing in working-class post-industrial areas that had returned to Labour in 2024. The scale of the defeat prompted immediate speculation about Keir Starmer's leadership and the government's ability to recover before the next general election. Deputy Prime Minister Angela Rayner, Health Secretary Wes Streeting, and Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham were named in reports as potential leadership contenders.

media.caption: Labour loses 35 councils and 1,300+ seats in historic May 2026 local elections defeat

title: Reform UK Wins 13 Councils and 1,350+ Seats — Displaces Conservatives as Dominant Right
detail: Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, recorded an unprecedented breakthrough in the 7 May 2026 local elections, winning more than 1,350 council seats and control of 13 councils across England — predominantly in coastal towns, post-industrial areas of the Midlands and North, and rural England. Farage declared the results a 'historic shift in British politics', effectively displacing the Conservatives as the dominant right-wing force in local government. The Conservatives themselves suffered further losses but were outperformed by Reform in many of their former heartlands, triggering a renewed debate within the party about whether to maintain a distinct electoral lane from Reform or attempt some form of realignment.

media.caption: Reform UK wins 13 councils in 2026 elections — Farage declares 'historic shift in British politics'

title: Starmer Vows to Stay On as PM Despite Worst Labour Election Losses in Years
detail: Prime Minister Keir Starmer publicly refused to resign following Labour's historic local election losses on 8 May 2026, stating he would 'get on with the job' and that the government's reform programme needed time to deliver results. Starmer acknowledged voter frustration but framed the results as a consequence of a difficult economic inheritance including a £22bn fiscal gap left by the previous Conservative government. His refusal to stand down did not quell speculation about internal party pressure, with Westminster sources pointing to potential challenges from within Cabinet in coming months if the polling did not improve.

media.caption: Starmer refuses to quit as PM despite historic Labour losses in May 2026 local elections

title: SNP Wins Fifth Consecutive Scottish Parliament Term; Swinney Revives IndyRef2 Push
detail: The Scottish National Party secured a fifth consecutive term running the Scottish government in the 7 May 2026 Scottish Parliament elections, though again without an outright majority. With Scottish Green Party support maintaining the pro-independence bloc's control of Holyrood, First Minister John Swinney pledged to bring forward a motion in the Scottish Parliament on its first sitting day to begin the process of seeking a Section 30 order from Westminster for an independence referendum — with a potential vote targeted for 2028. Labour's catastrophic result in England simultaneously weakened Starmer's political authority to block such a request and emboldened the independence movement, reigniting one of the most serious constitutional questions facing the UK.

media.caption: SNP wins fifth term; Swinney revives Scottish independence referendum push, targeting 2028
